discovery_health.diagnosis: The free public discovery chain is non-zero and now has its first intentional same-author/similar-age comparison candidate. PUBLIC_X_AGGREGATOR remains the highest-yield route, while AUTHOR_WATCH now also has one admitted recent sample. Direct X rendering remains unavailable.

cohort_definitions.recent: Unique real X status permalinks with published_at sufficient for a 0-48h freshness classification.
cohort_definitions.interaction_observed: Recent posts with at least one labeled public interaction observation or aggregate interaction observation. This cohort is not equivalent to high-view.
cohort_definitions.high_distribution: Posts with verifiable distribution evidence such as views >=10000 under the feed contract. None are fully verified in the current unique sample.
cohort_definitions.matched_comparison_candidate: A same-author or similar-author/status-age comparison selected to reduce confounding. It is not automatically a low-distribution control.
cohort_definitions.control: Ordinary or low-distribution posts matched as closely as possible on author scale, topic and post age, with comparable distribution evidence. None are available yet.

comparison_pairs.shared_context: Same official author, same day, similar AI/Claude product-update topic, both original posts.
comparison_pairs.structural_difference: The Managed Agents post explains a capability and orchestration mechanism; the Projects post leads with immediate access expansion plus a short walkthrough.
comparison_pairs.note: Public mirrors show raw numeric sequences for both posts, but their positions are not independently labeled. The pair can be used for qualitative structure comparison but not high-vs-low distribution inference yet.

structure_labels.label: IMMEDIATE_PRODUCT_OR_ACCESS_CHANGE
structure_labels.description: The post gives readers a concrete new capability, access change or immediately usable product update.

structure_labels.label: SPECIFIC_HIGH_STAKES_SAFETY_CLAIM
structure_labels.description: The post centers a concrete model-behavior or control/safety claim with potentially high consequences.

structure_labels.label: CONCRETE_NOUNS_AND_ACTIONS
structure_labels.description: All six excerpts are anchored in a named product, actor, capability or policy action rather than generic opinion.

candidate_patterns.name: Concrete utility or access change may create a strong reader payoff
candidate_patterns.support: Four of the six fresh unique posts frame a specific capability/access change. They are easy to understand and give the reader an immediate answer to what changed or what is now possible.
candidate_patterns.limitations: Most are official or very large AI accounts, there is no verified low-distribution control, and some records lack labeled reach metrics. The same-author pair is not yet distribution-classifiable.

candidate_patterns.name: Specific high-stakes claims can create information value without a lifestyle/self-mirroring hook
candidate_patterns.support: Two fresh posts lead with concrete AI safety/control claims. This is useful negative evidence against treating self-mirroring as a necessary condition for attention.
candidate_patterns.limitations: Only Anthropic has labeled interaction observations in the current sample; Satya Nadella's record has no verified reach metric. Author authority is a major confounder.

counterexamples.point: An official Google AI announcement has labeled engagement but materially lower observed likes/reposts than the Anthropic behavior-report post. Being an official AI account and announcing something new is therefore not sufficient by itself to explain stronger interaction.

Conflicting untimed third-party engagement observations show why apparent numeric precision from mirrors can be misleading. The canonical likes/reposts remain null rather than selecting the more convenient snapshot.

A well-matched same-author pair exists, but unlabeled mirror number positions prevent a valid high-vs-low classification. Matching author and time alone is not enough; comparable distribution evidence is still required.

confounders: All six admitted fresh unique posts are from globally prominent technology executives or official AI/product accounts; author scale is still poorly controlled outside the single ClaudeDevs pair.
No verified ordinary/low-distribution control cohort exists yet.
Most posts lack verified view counts; interaction observations cannot be equated with total distribution.
Direct X rendering is blocked in the current environment, so most metrics come from provenance-scoped public aggregators or corroborating sources.
Third-party caches can lag and may not expose metric snapshot times. Source freshness is explicitly gated, but raw unlabeled mirror sequences cannot be interpreted as named metrics.
The admitted sample is still heavily concentrated in AI/technology. Four current Chinese-language leads exist, but remain outside the canonical sample until original status IDs are resolved.
recent_changes: The feed now contains six unique recent X status IDs across five runs.
AUTHOR_WATCH produced its first admitted recent sample by deliberately searching for a same-author comparison around an existing ClaudeDevs post.
The first matched comparison pair reduces author/time confounding but remains distribution-unclassified because mirror metrics are unlabeled.
Four current Chinese-language discovery leads were preserved in a sidecar instead of being discarded or incorrectly promoted without original status IDs.
Source freshness policy separates post time, source snapshot time and metric observation time.
next_sampling_priorities: Resolve the original X status IDs for the four current Chinese-language leads and admit only those whose identity/time can be corroborated.
For each strong fresh sample, attempt at least one same-author ±24h comparison before falling back to similar-author scale/topic/age.
Find labeled distribution evidence for the ClaudeDevs pair; until then do not call either member a high- or low-distribution control.
Grow the fresh canonical set to at least 10-20 additional real status IDs before attempting replicated structural claims.
Expand beyond AI/official-company accounts into Chinese tech creators, ordinary-person experience, work/money, social observation, reversal/oddity and history/culture buckets.
Prefer sources that expose an exact status permalink plus explicitly labeled metrics and a trustworthy source snapshot time; downgrade generic aggregator pages with stale-cache risk.
Seek verifiable view counts, but do not weaken evidence rules or buy a paid data source to obtain them.
note: Discovery and comparison sampling are now functioning. The next bottleneck is not finding posts; it is resolving diverse Chinese originals and obtaining comparable distribution evidence for matched pairs without inferring unlabeled mirror metrics.
